chapter: Wartime South and the Ernie Fields band
title: Hearing the new Billy Eckstine band in Florida
summary: He hears Eckstine's band days after forming, with Parker, Dizzy, Blakey, Sarah and Lucky Thompson.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: So I had some great times there in Tampa. And this is where I also heard the Billy Eckstine band, the fourth day it was together. That's when he had Sarah, and in the reed section they had Charlie Parker playing the lead, and a little kid named Junior out of Kansas City playing the other also [JOHN JACKSON], Lucky Thompson was playing tenor, Leo Parker was playing the baritone, Art Blakey was on drums, Tommy Potter played the bass, and John Malachi on the piano. And in the trumpet section they had Gail Brockman playing

the lead, and Dizzy Gillespie... That's when Dizzy was really schooling Art Blakey. That was the early Bebop period; he was really schooling Art how to play with the band. And Benny Harris, a fine trumpet player, was with the band. Now, he's the one that "Ornithology," the tune that's based on "How High The Moon" changes that became famous through the era. It was a terrific band.
